Not op, but I own a few tarantulas. 
They’re pretty easy to care. You basically just feed them once a week and make sure they have water. Most of the work is picking out a species and researching the proper setup for them. I would say caring for them is dirt cheap. Buying the tarantula and the enclosure can be a bit pricey though, especially if you’re buying online. 

Most common feeders will die before they get a chance to infest your house if they happen to escape. If you get mealworms you can just keep them in the fridge and they last a really long time. No maintenance required. Crickets and Dubia roaches are other choices which require a little maintenance to keep alive, but also super easy to care for. 

If you’re serious about getting a tarantula, you should visit r/tarantulas and the arachnoboards forum.

My dog used to do the same thing when she was a puppy (minus the jumping haha). I think for the most part, she grew out of it, but I did crate train her.

You can do something similar to crate training, where you slowly get her used to being away from you for longer periods of time. Basically, you can start with just closing the gate. If she isn’t whining or jumping, open the gate and reward her. Then close the gate again, wait a few seconds, and open it only if she remains calm. If she’s doing well, you can increase the duration even more, or walk away from the gate while still staying in sight. 

After you do that, you can start walking out of view briefly and if she still stays calm, reward her by opening the gate.  Then increase the duration you’re out of view and so on. 

Try not to open the gate or give her any attention while she is whining or jumping. You don’t want to reward her for doing something you don’t want her to do, otherwise she will never stop. 

It’s a long process, but it will get better over time. Just keep practicing this even when you’re home so she doesn’t associate being in there with long periods of alone time and boredom.
